> **Beta.** This is the first release of Fractal JDT LS, and it's a beta. It passes its full test suite against the pinned JDT LS 1.63.0, but no client has used it day to day yet, and this tag is the first real run of the release workflow. Expect rough edges: report them as [issues](https://github.com/nokesc/fractal-jdtls/issues). Its install layout, launcher options and agent behavior may still change. The version keeps the `<JDT LS version>-<n>` scheme, so fixes and the first non-beta release come as `v1.63.0-2` or later, never as a renamed tag.

The first release of Fractal JDT LS. It installs the official Eclipse JDT Language Server 1.63.0 and adds a launcher, a drop-in for the stock `jdtls`, that starts it with a small Java agent. The agent keeps each Git worktree's Maven projects separate when several worktrees of one project share one JDT LS process.

**Linux only.** Needs Python 3.10 or newer and a JDK 21 or newer. See the [README](https://github.com/nokesc/fractal-jdtls#readme) for installing and using it.

## What's pinned

| Component | Version | Verified against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eclipse JDT LS | 1.63.0 (`jdt-language-server-1.63.0-202610191322.tar.gz`) | SHA-256 `b1f2abe0b3cccb462cf64fb4a5587c7d09df60cf8be7748b152cbd89d018bdc4`, equal to Eclipse's published `.sha256`; plus the SHA-256 of each of its 124 files |
| m2e (bundled in JDT LS) | core `2.8.0.20260815-0704`, jdt `2.5.300.20260813-1359`, embedded Maven `3.9.16` | the tarball's checksum only (see below) |
| Byte Buddy | 1.18.14, from Maven Central | SHA-256 `b7f2b2f111c6ddc09d3d9718ca5895dde16217bb4e5f2d2a6eb571f274909a82`, equal to Central's published `.sha512`, `.sha256` and `.sha1` |
| Java | 21 or newer, JDT LS 1.63.0's minimum | the launcher refuses an older one |

The zip holds only this project's files: `bin/install.py`, `bin/jdtls`, the agent and boot jars, `pin.json`, `release-files.json`, `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. The installer downloads JDT LS from `download.eclipse.org` and Byte Buddy from Maven Central, and verifies every file before installing. Nothing from Eclipse or Byte Buddy is redistributed.

Tested together: the agent's JUnit tests, the installer's and launcher's unit tests, and an integration suite that installs this zip and runs real JDT LS 1.63.0 on a main checkout and two linked worktrees of one Maven project. Each worktree resolves its own modules after import, edits, reimport and restart; without the agent, the same fixture fails with m2e's duplicate-coordinates error.

## How each downloaded file is trusted

`pin.json` holds the SHA-256 of every file, so an install can be re-checked at any time (`install.py --verify`), and the launcher checks it on every start. What each file *should* be comes from outside checks, recorded in the [pin report](https://github.com/nokesc/fractal-jdtls/blob/v1.63.0-1/.context/pins/1.63.0.md):

- **Eclipse signs only some of JDT LS.** 58 of the 110 jars in `plugins/`, and the one jar in `features/`, are signed by the Eclipse Foundation (`jarsigner -verify`).
- **41 jars are byte-identical to artifacts on Maven Central.**
- **Eclipse publishes no PGP signature for the tarball,** only its SHA-256.
- **29 jars and 13 other files are trusted only through that checksum.** Nothing else vouches for them:
  - all of m2e: `org.eclipse.m2e.core`, `org.eclipse.m2e.jdt`, `org.eclipse.m2e.maven.runtime` and `org.eclipse.m2e.apt.core`. This m2e build isn't on m2e's signed update sites.
  - `com.sun.jna_5.19.1.v20260612-1000`, `org.eclipse.jdt.core.javac_1.0.0.z20260430-1959` and the wrapped decompiler engine;
  - 21 wrapped flexmark jars and `wrapped.org.jetbrains.annotations`;
  - the scripts and configuration: `bin/jdtls`, `bin/jdtls.bat`, `bin/jdtls.py` and the ten `config_*/config.ini` files. The launcher never runs Eclipse's `bin/jdtls` scripts; it uses `config_linux/config.ini` as JDT LS's shared configuration.
- **Byte Buddy's PGP signature (`.asc`) wasn't checked when it was pinned:** the signer's key (`7999BEFBA1039E8B`) wasn't in the maintainer's keyring. Byte Buddy is trusted through Maven Central's published hashes.

## Known gaps

- **Adding and removing workspace folders at runtime** (`workspace/didChangeWorkspaceFolders`) isn't tested. The worktrees a server should hold are tested only as the folders it starts with.
- **The agent must be present on every start.** A workspace created without it keeps its projects' unprefixed names, and resolves across worktrees again. To start using the agent with an existing workspace, give JDT LS a fresh `-data`.
- **Worktree folder names must be unique** among the worktrees that share one JDT LS process. Projects are named `<worktree folder>.<artifactId>`; the agent reports a collision but can't resolve it.
- **Version-pinned hooks.** The agent hooks private methods of m2e and Maven in this JDT LS build. It reports any hook that isn't in place, on stderr and in the JDT LS log, but a different JDT LS needs a new release of this project.
- Linux only. Gradle, classifiers and version ranges aren't tested.

Report a problem: <https://github.com/nokesc/fractal-jdtls/issues>.
